subject: Incident response playbook: notice windows, subprocessor handoffs and data transit
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cypresstech.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: legal@cypresstech.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA incident timelines and subprocessor handoffs

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this. Our procurement and security teams reviewed the draft DPA and have two primary asks related to incident notification and subprocessors:

1) Tighten the initial notification window — they prefer an explicit 24-hour "acknowledgement" and a 48-hour substantive notification for confirmed customer-impacting incidents (PII/exposure).

2) Clarify the handoff to subprocessors: when we request evidence/logs, what is the expected timeline for Redwood to obtain and transmit subprocessor evidence? We are particularly sensitive to cross-border transfers: will Redwood provide a chain-of-custody and confirm whether subprocessors keep logs within the EU for EU-origin data?

Attached is a spreadsheet with the procurement questions and examples. Can you confirm what you can commit to contractually versus operationally (e.g., progress updates every 24 hrs until resolution)?

Best,
Elena

[Attachment: cypress-dpa-questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cypresstech.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA incident timelines and subprocessor handoffs

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and the spreadsheet. High level answers below; Marissa/Neha are looped for legal/forensic specifics.

- Standard Redwood DPA: we provide an initial "alert" within 72 hours of confirming an incident that impacts Customer Data, and we aim to provide substantive notification (scope and available evidence) within 7 days. The 72/7 cadence is our baseline for hosted customers to allow for initial forensics.

- Operational commitments: we can provide operational status updates every 24 hours once an incident is open. We can also include an "acknowledgement" receipt within 24 hours of initial triage on a best-effort basis; however, making a contractual 24-hour substantive-notice commitment for all incident types is challenging because some investigations require coordination with subprocessors and law enforcement.

- Subprocessors & evidence: Redwood maintains a current subprocessor roster (we'll attach). When Cypress requests evidence that resides with a subprocessor, we will: 1) request the evidence from the subprocessor immediately; 2) provide a timeline for when we expect the subprocessor's response; 3) escalate if the subprocessor's response is delayed. Typical turnaround for cooperative evidence requests is 48-120 hours depending on the subprocessor and jurisdiction.

- Cross-border: for EU-origin data we will prioritize subprocessors with EU data processing capabilities; if logs must cross borders we provide appropriate transfer/legal mechanisms (SCCs, contractual safeguards) and will document the transfer chain for the customer.

Next steps: Marissa and Neha, can you propose contract language options (48 vs 72 hour windows, and a clause for prioritized handling of PII) and confirm the fastest operational evidence turnaround we can promise for our major subprocessors? Elena — would you be available for a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0182

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, Elena Soto <elena.soto@cypresstech.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA incident timelines and subprocessor handoffs

Elena — appreciate the detailed ask. A few legal/operational points and suggested DPA language below.

1) Acknowledgement vs substantive notice:
- We can contractually commit to an "acknowledgement" of receipt of a reported incident within 24 hours of Redwood's detection/confirmation (this can be a short-form email confirming triage has begun).
- For "substantive notice" (root cause, impacted data sets, initial scope), we can offer two options to include as selectable DPA language:
  Option 1 (Standard): Substantive notice within 72 hours of confirmation.
  Option 2 (High-sensitivity): Substantive notice within 48 hours for incidents impacting defined high-sensitivity datasets (PII, health identifiers) where Customer has flagged the data class in the contract.

2) Evidence & subprocessor handoff:
- Clause: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain evidence from subprocessors and provide the Customer with a status timeline. Where the subprocessor is subject to local legal constraints, Redwood will document limits and provide available summaries.
- Operationally, our current median for cooperative evidence retrieval from core subprocessors is ~72 hours. For high-priority requests we can escalate to 48 hours for a subset of vendors provided we include that roster in an annex.

3) Data transit and chain-of-custody:
- We will include a transfer log excerpt and a subprocessor-confirmation statement as part of the evidence package when feasible. We cannot, however, guarantee that all raw forensic logs will remain in-region unless the customer has a private/dedicated deployment with pinned hardware or a contractual requirement to restrict subprocessor transfers.

Attachments: subprocessor roster (current), redlined DPA options (vA) with the opt-in 48-hour clause and an escalation SLA.

Proposed contract language (short):
"Upon confirmation of a Security Incident impacting Customer Data, Redwood shall: (a) acknowledge receipt within 24 hours; (b) provide a substantive notification within [48/72] hours as selected by Customer; and (c) provide status updates at least every 24 hours until the incident is closed. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and transmit evidence held by its subprocessors and will document any legal or technical limits on such transfers."

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: subprocessor-roster-2026.csv]

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cypresstech.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: legal@cypresstech.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA incident timelines and subprocessor handoffs

Marissa / Jasmine — thanks, that language is helpful. A couple follow-ups:

- Cypress procurement insists on a contractual 24-hour acknowledgement clause (we can accept that as "acknowledgement only"). They are pushing for a 48-hour substantive notice for any confirmed exposure of PII; if Redwood cannot agree to 48 for all, we'll need a clear list of which datasets qualify for 48-hour handling.

- On subprocessors: we need confirmation that Redwood will provide the chain-of-custody and indicate whether KMS/HSM audit logs can be included when the evidence involves encryption keys or access records. If not available, note that explicitly.

Can we get a redline of the DPA with the two options called out (48/72) and a proposed annex that lists the subset of subprocessors Redwood will commit to 48-hr evidence turnaround for? Procurement would also like a short sample timeline in the contract (e.g., T+0 acknowledgement, T+24 status, T+48 substantive or T+72 substantive depending on selection).

Regards,
Elena

[Attachment: procurement-summary.docx]

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cypresstech.com>, jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA incident timelines and subprocessor handoffs

Elena — quick operational note from GtM/CS side: we are comfortable committing to the 24-hour acknowledgement in contract and to daily updates in the SLA. For substantive notice, we propose the following compromise for the DPA redline:

- Contract: 24-hour acknowledgement (T+0), daily status at least every 24 hours while open.
- Substantive notification: Redwood will provide initial substantive notification within 72 hours by default. For customers that select the High-sensitivity option and specify the affected data classes in the contract annex, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide substantive notification within 48 hours.

Operational caveat: where evidence is held exclusively by a subprocessor and subject to third-party legal restrictions, Redwood will provide the customer a documented timeline for expected delivery of evidence and will escalate internally. We can also offer a dedicated escalation liaison (Neha Kapoor) for Cypress to use if the matter is time-sensitive.

I will coordinate a short one-page mutual action plan to attach to the redline so procurement sees the practical steps and timelines.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: MAP-cypress-incident-handling.pdf]

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA incident timelines and subprocessor handoffs

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and patience. We will produce a redlined DPA that contains:

1) A contractual 24-hour acknowledgement clause (T+0).
2) Two selectable substantive-notice options: 72 hours (standard) or 48 hours (high-sensitivity datasets listed in a contract annex).
3) A requirement that Redwood provide status updates at least every 24 hours while the incident remains open.
4) An evidence-handling annex explaining our subprocessor roster, target cooperative evidence turnarounds (48-72 hours for prioritized vendors), and a statement on cross-border transfers and SCCs.

We will attach: the redline (redwood-dpa-options-vA.pdf), current subprocessor roster (subprocessor-roster-2026.csv), and a short mutual action plan that maps the timeline items to operational owners. Please confirm availability for a 30-min sync Monday 10/26 or Tuesday 10/27 so we can walk the redline and the annex.

Thanks,
Jasmine
